title: Retract supplied by a proper surjection
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism of schemes [def-weil-surjective-morphism] (no properness is needed), let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring (in the application $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$; $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ gives abelian sheaves), and for a scheme $T$ let $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant sheaf of rings $\underline\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $f^{-1}:\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $f_*:\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], with the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Let $I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $J$ an object of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $j:f^{-1}I\to J$ a monomorphism of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ (in the application $J$ is injective; that is not used here). Then the adjoint map $\iota=f_*(j)\circ\eta_I:I\to f_*J$ of $j$ ($\eta$ the unit of the adjunction) is a monomorphism, and there is a morphism $\rho:f_*J\to I$ with $\rho\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_I$; hence $I$ is a direct summand of $f_*J$: $(\rho,\ \pi):f_*J\xrightarrow{\sim}I\oplus\ker\rho$, where $\pi$ is the map to $\ker\rho$ induced by $\mathrm{id}-\iota\rho$.

proof.text: *The adjoint map and the triangle identity.* By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (3), $f^{-1}:\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is left adjoint to $f_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; let $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon:f^{-1}f_*\to\mathrm{id}$ be unit and counit. The adjoint of $j$ is $\iota=f_*(j)\circ\eta_I$, and the adjunction bijection being inverse to $\psi\mapsto\varepsilon_J\circ f^{-1}(\psi)$, we have the triangle identity $j=\varepsilon_J\circ f^{-1}(\iota)$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an injective map of sheaves $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ ... Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$.") ('the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$' is the adjoint of $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$)

proof.text: *Passing to abelian sheaves.* In $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ kernels are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], as they are in $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]; since a morphism of an abelian category is a monomorphism iff its kernel is zero, a morphism of $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is a monomorphism iff its underlying morphism of abelian sheaves is one. The underlying abelian sheaf of $f^{-1}G$ is the abelian inverse image of that of $G$ ([prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2)), and that of $f_*F$ is the abelian direct image $W\mapsto F(W\times_YX)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. So, writing the same letters for underlying abelian sheaves and maps, $j:f^{-1}I\to J$ is a monomorphism of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$, the identity $j=\varepsilon_J\circ f^{-1}(\iota)$ of step 1 holds in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ (with $\varepsilon_J$ now just some morphism $f^{-1}f_*J\to J$ of abelian sheaves), and it suffices to show that $\iota:I\to f_*J$ is a monomorphism of $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an injective map of sheaves $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ ... Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$."); the reduction of injectivity of a map of module sheaves to the underlying abelian sheaves is written out here

proof.text: *Geometric points above the points of $Y$.* For every point $x\in X$ choose an algebraic closure $\Omega_x$ of the residue field $\kappa(x)$; the point $x$ with $\kappa(x)\to\Omega_x$ is a geometric point $\bar x_x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_x\to X$ lying over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\bar y_x=f\circ\bar x_x$ is a geometric point of $Y$ lying over $f(x)$. The images of the $\bar x_x$ ($x\in X$) cover $X$, and since $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] the images $f(x)$ of the $\bar y_x$ cover $Y$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an injective map of sheaves $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ ... Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$.") ('Since $f$ is surjective ... look at stalks in geometric points'); this is where surjectivity is used, and only surjectivity

proof.text:
*The stalk computation.* Fix $x\in X$ and write $\bar x=\bar x_x$, $\bar y=\bar y_x=f\circ\bar x$. By [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] there are isomorphisms $\theta_G:(f^{-1}G)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\bar y}$ of stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], natural in the abelian sheaf $G$ on $Y_{\Et}$; naturality at $\iota:I\to f_*J$ gives $(f^{-1}\iota)_{\bar x}=\theta_{f_*J}^{-1}\circ\iota_{\bar y}\circ\theta_I$. Taking stalks at $\bar x$ (a functor) in the identity $j=\varepsilon_J\circ f^{-1}(\iota)$ of step 2 gives
$$j_{\bar x}\circ\theta_I^{-1}=\bigl((\varepsilon_J)_{\bar x}\circ\theta_{f_*J}^{-1}\bigr)\circ\iota_{\bar y}:\ I_{\bar y}\to J_{\bar x}.$$
That is: the stalk map $I_{\bar y}\to(f_*J)_{\bar y}$ followed by the map $(f_*J)_{\bar y}\to J_{\bar x}$ is the stalk at $\bar x$ of the inclusion $f^{-1}I\to J$, read through $I_{\bar y}=(f^{-1}I)_{\bar x}$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an injective map of sheaves $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ ... Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$.") ('look at stalks in geometric points', written out); the stalk of an inverse image is the closed node lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar

proof.text: *Injectivity on stalks, hence $\iota$ monic.* Since $j$ is a monomorphism of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ and the $\bar x_x$ cover $X$ (step 3), [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono] (the 'only if' direction) shows that every $j_{\bar x_x}$ is injective; so the left side of the identity of step 4 is injective, hence so is $\iota_{\bar y_x}$ (if $g\circ h$ is injective, $h$ is injective). Thus $\iota$ is injective on the stalks at the family $(\bar y_x)_{x\in X}$, whose images cover $Y$ (step 3), and [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono] (the 'if' direction) shows that $\iota$ is a monomorphism of $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$, hence of $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ by step 2.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Theorem 03PU (label theorem-exactness-stalks: a map of sheaves is injective iff injective on all geometric stalks), used as in Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an injective map of sheaves $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ ... Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$.")

proof.text: *The retraction.* $I$ is injective in $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and $\iota:I\to f_*J$ is a monomorphism (step 5), so $\mathrm{Hom}(f_*J,I)\to\mathrm{Hom}(I,I)$, $\rho\mapsto\rho\circ\iota$, is surjective; a preimage $\rho$ of $\mathrm{id}_I$ satisfies $\rho\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_I$. (In Mathlib: CategoryTheory.Injective.factorThru (𝟙 I) ι with Injective.comp_factorThru.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an injective map of sheaves $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ ... Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$.") ('Since $\mathcal I$ is injective')

proof.text: *Direct summand.* In the abelian category $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $e=\mathrm{id}-\iota\rho$ is an endomorphism of $f_*J$ with $\rho e=\rho-\rho\iota\rho=0$, so $e$ factors as $f_*J\xrightarrow{\pi}\ker\rho\hookrightarrow f_*J$; the maps $(\rho,\pi):f_*J\to I\oplus\ker\rho$ and $(\iota,\ \mathrm{incl}):I\oplus\ker\rho\to f_*J$ are mutually inverse (using $\rho\iota=\mathrm{id}$, $\pi\iota=0$ since $e\iota=\iota-\iota=0$, $\rho|_{\ker\rho}=0$, $\pi|_{\ker\rho}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\iota\rho+e=\mathrm{id}$). So $I$ is a direct summand of $f_*J$.

Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$.") ('we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$')

split_report.summary: Statement fixed: the coefficient category named as in lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change (sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf of a commutative ring Λ on the small etale site; Λ=F_r in the application, Λ=Z abelian sheaves); 'proper' dropped (Stacks 0A4C uses only that f is surjective, and the proof uses no more); 'surjective' repointed from def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions to def-weil-surjective-morphism; the adjoint map named (f_*(j)∘η_I) and the retraction ρ with ρι=id stated, which is what lemma-weil-pbc-cancellation step 2 uses; injectivity of J dropped as unused (any monomorphism f^{-1}I→J). stmt_deps: removed def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions and def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks (stalks are not in the statement); added the module category, the adjunction and def-sp-injective-resolutions. Proof written out from Stacks 0A4C, first paragraph ('look at stalks in geometric points') in seven steps: triangle identity of the adjunction (prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact); reduction to underlying abelian sheaves; a covering family of geometric points x̄_x (algebraic closures of residue fields) whose images f∘x̄_x cover Y by surjectivity (no separate 'surjective on geometric points' lemma or 04FN needed); stalk computation by the closed lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar; the monomorphism criterion on a covering family of geometric stalks (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono, Stacks 03PU; the closed lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative covers isomorphisms only and is no longer used); retraction from injectivity of I; direct summand. The existence of an injective J (lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives) is used by the citer lemma-weil-pbc-cancellation, not here.
